original_description: Drive interactive command-line REPLs and long-running interactive processes through tmux — send input, wait until the program is actually ready, and read its output back programmatically. Use whenever you need to interact with a running interactive process rather than run a one-shot command: a Python/Node/psql/irb/sqlite REPL, an SSH session, a TUI, a debugger (gdb/pdb), or a nested `claude` session. Trigger phrases: "drive a REPL", "test in a tmux session", "interact with a running interactive process", "feed input to a process on stdin", "automate a CLI that prompts", "send-keys / capture-pane". Covers tmux send-keys (and the literal-text vs Enter/C-m gotcha), capture-pane reads, a wait_for_prompt readiness poller, and session lifecycle (new-session/new-window/detach/kill-session). NOT for one-shot non-interactive shell commands — run those directly with the Bash tool; reach for this only when a process stays open and exchanges input/output across multiple steps.
best_description: Use this skill whenever a command-line program stays open and you need to exchange input and output with it across multiple steps — instead of running one-shot commands that exit. This is the right tool the moment a user wants to: keep a session alive and run several commands in it reading output between each; start or reuse a REPL (python, node, irb, psql, sqlite3) and feed it statements one at a time, checking each result before the next; hold an SSH session open across commands; step through a debugger (gdb/pdb); or automate any CLI that prompts and waits. It applies equally whether the process is one you launch now or one already running in a tmux pane (e.g. "psql is open in pane 0:0.1, run these SELECTs"). It works by driving the process through tmux — send keystrokes, poll until the program is actually ready, capture the output back. Do NOT use it for a single command that runs and exits, a file read, or editing config — run those directly with Bash.

i started irb in tmux, send it a few ruby expressions and read the values back without killing the repl
drive an interactive sqlite3 session: create the table, insert the seed rows, run the aggregate, and give me the exact number it prints

spin up a python3 repl and feed it these 4 pandas snippets one at a time, check each result before sending the next
read /var/log/nginx/error.log and summarize the 500s from this morning
install tmux and zsh on this fresh ubuntu box
run the full test suite with pytest -q and tell me if anything fails
ssh to prod and run systemctl restart api then disconnect
